title: Comparer des quantités et des qualités
summary: Compare nouns, build complex superlatives and distinguish subjective superlative judgement from factual reporting.
objectives: Use `plus/moins/autant de` with nouns and `que` for the comparison.
Build superlatives with appropriate agreement, position and comparison group.
Choose a subjunctive superlative relative for evaluation while preserving legitimate indicative assertions.

sources.label: Public complex-superlative lesson consulted for benchmark scope

sections.title: Compare how much or how many with `de`
paragraphs: Before a noun, use `plus de` (more), `moins de` (less/fewer), `autant de` (as much/as many), then `que` to introduce the comparison. The noun can be countable or uncountable: `plus de sièges`, `moins de bruit`, `autant d'énergie`. `De` elides before a vowel; do not turn it into `des` simply because the noun is plural.

For adjectives and adverbs, equality uses `aussi`, not `autant de`: `aussi rapide`, `aussi vite`. With a verb by itself, use `autant`: `elle travaille autant que moi`. A precise difference can use `de plus/de moins` after the quantity: `deux places de plus`. `Plus de vingt` means more than twenty, a threshold rather than a two-group comparison.
points: An unambiguous comparison names the same measure on both sides; more rooms does not itself mean a bigger total area.

examples.french: Cette salle a **plus de sièges que** l'autre.
examples.english: This room has more seats than the other one.

examples.french: Le nouveau moteur fait **moins de bruit que** l'ancien.
examples.english: The new engine makes less noise than the old one.

examples.french: Nous avons **autant de travail que** vous.
examples.english: We have as much work as you.

examples.french: Il nous faut deux chaises **de plus**.
examples.note: An added quantity, not `plus de` + noun.

mistakes.avoid: Nous avons aussi de dossiers que vous.
mistakes.prefer: Nous avons autant de dossiers que vous.
mistakes.why: Equality with a noun uses `autant de`; `aussi` compares adjectives or adverbs.

sections.title: Comparer les mêmes choses ou deux catégories
paragraphs: After `que`, ask what the comparison is between. `Cette agence reçoit plus de demandes que la nôtre` compares the number of requests received by two agencies; the noun `demandes` is understood on the second side. `Cette agence reçoit plus de demandes que de réponses` compares two kinds of thing within one agency. Repeat `de` before the second noun category, including elision before a vowel.

A short comparison can end in a stressed pronoun: `autant de travail que moi`. A full clause is also possible and may be clearer when subjects, times or actions differ. Repeating the verb is not forbidden. Keep enough information to show who has, receives or does what; brevity is useful only when the missing material is recoverable.
points: The measure and the comparison target are separate choices: two owners of the same resource, or two resource categories.

examples.french: Notre antenne reçoit **plus de demandes que la vôtre**.
examples.english: Our branch receives more requests than yours.
examples.note: Two branches, one kind of thing counted.

examples.french: Notre antenne reçoit **plus de demandes que de réponses**.
examples.english: Our branch receives more requests than replies.
examples.note: One branch, two categories. `De` appears before both nouns.

examples.french: Elle a **autant de responsabilités que moi**.
examples.english: She has as many responsibilities as I do.
examples.note: The short second part uses stressed `moi`, not subject `je`.

examples.french: Nous avons reçu **moins de candidatures que nous en avions reçu l'an dernier**.
examples.english: We received fewer applications than we had received last year.
examples.note: A full comparison clause makes the earlier time explicit; repeating `recevoir` is grammatical.

mistakes.avoid: Il y a plus de questions que réponses.
mistakes.prefer: Il y a plus de questions que de réponses.
mistakes.why: The comparison is between two noun quantities, so `de` is repeated before the second category.

sections.title: Specify the comparison group and keep agreement
paragraphs: A superlative ranks something at an extreme within a set: the most/least useful room in the building. With an adjective normally after the noun, a clear pattern is definite article + noun + `le/la/les plus/moins` + agreeing adjective + `de` + comparison group. The noun's article and the superlative article may both appear: `la salle la plus lumineuse du bâtiment`.

Common pre-noun adjectives can stay before the noun: `le plus grand parc du quartier`. Ordinal rankings add `premier`, `deuxième`, `troisième`, etc.: `la deuxième plus grande salle de la ville`. The comparison set is introduced by `de`, with normal contractions or proper-name usage: `de la ville`, `du pays`, `des trois`, `de France`.

Agreement forms: `le plus utile, la plus utile, les plus utiles`; `le moins cher, la moins chère, les moins chers/chères`. `Bon`'s comparative/superlative uses `meilleur/meilleure/meilleurs/meilleures`. `Mieux` compares `bien`, not a noun's adjective. `Mauvais` can give `plus mauvais` or `pire`, with nuance; `pire` often intensifies a negative judgement and is not the only permitted form.

When comparing degrees of the same subject across times or circumstances rather than ranking different entities, `le plus/le moins` can remain invariable: `c'est le matin qu'elle est le plus attentive`. The adjective still agrees with the subject. This is different from `elle est la plus attentive du groupe`, which ranks her among people.

examples.french: C'est **la salle la plus lumineuse du** bâtiment.
examples.english: It is the brightest room in the building.

examples.french: Voici **les deux itinéraires les moins longs de** notre sélection.
examples.english: Here are the two shortest routes in our selection.
examples.note: Plural superlative and explicit comparison set.

examples.french: C'est **la deuxième plus grande ville de** la région.
examples.english: It is the second-largest city in the region.
examples.note: Ordinal ranking with a pre-noun adjective.

examples.french: Ces horaires sont **meilleurs** pour les familles.
examples.english: These opening hours are better for families.

examples.french: C'est après une pause qu'elle est **le plus attentive**.
examples.english: She is most attentive after a break.
examples.note: Her own varying attention, not a ranking of different women.

mistakes.avoid: C'est la solution le plus simple du groupe.
mistakes.prefer: C'est la solution la plus simple du groupe.
mistakes.why: Ranking this feminine `solution` among several solutions requires `la plus`.

sections.title: A superlative often invites evaluation, not an automatic tense rule
paragraphs: After a superlative, a relative clause often uses the subjunctive when expressing a personal evaluation, an extreme judgement or the limits of one's experience: `le meilleur conseil que j'aie reçu`. For an already experienced event, the past subjunctive is common: `aie/ait/ayons...` + participle. `Jamais` in an affirmative experiential comparison means ever; it does not need `ne` and does not mean never here.

The indicative is also legitimate when the relative clause simply identifies or asserts a fact: `le plus grand des bâtiments que nous avons mesurés`. Even after a direct superlative, indicative can present factual experience rather than emphasizing evaluation. Do not reject it merely because `le plus` appears earlier. A constrained exercise must specify the intended mood or evaluative stance.

Agreement still applies: `la meilleure idée que j'aie entendue` has a preceding feminine direct object. The present subjunctive is appropriate for a current capacity or possibility: `la solution la moins chère que nous puissions proposer`.

examples.french: C'est le conseil le plus utile que j'**aie jamais reçu**.
examples.english: It is the most useful advice I have ever received.
examples.note: An evaluative limit of personal experience; `jamais` means ever.

examples.french: C'est la proposition la plus claire que nous **ayons lue**.
examples.english: It is the clearest proposal we have read.

examples.french: C'est l'option la moins chère que nous **puissions proposer**.
examples.english: It is the cheapest option we can offer.
examples.note: A present possibility, not completed experience.

examples.french: C'est le plus haut des trois bâtiments que nous **avons mesurés** hier.
examples.english: It is the tallest of the three buildings we measured yesterday.
examples.note: The indicative clause establishes the factual set being ranked.

practice.prompt: Compare two categories. Supply the missing preposition: Le comité a reçu autant de critiques que ___ suggestions.
practice.explanation: Both quantities are nouns; repeat de before the second category.

practice.prompt: What is compared in Cette équipe dispose de moins de véhicules que l'équipe voisine?
choices: The vehicle counts of two teams.
Vehicles and teams as two object categories.
answers: The vehicle counts of two teams.
practice.explanation: The second team's vehicle quantity is understood.

practice.prompt: Compare categories, with necessary elision: Le rapport contient plus de chiffres que ___ explications.
practice.explanation: Repeat de before the second category and elide before explications.

practice.prompt: The comparison stops after the pronoun. Supply the stressed form meaning I do: Tu as autant de réunions que ___.
practice.explanation: Use stressed moi in this short comparison; a finite clause would need its own subject and verb.

practice.prompt: A full comparison clause is intended. Supply avoir in the present: L'association a plus de matériel que nous en ___ nous-mêmes.
practice.explanation: The repeated verb is grammatical and makes the second holder explicit; en represents the quantity of equipment.

practice.prompt: Which sentence compares two kinds of publication, rather than two shops?
choices: Cette librairie vend plus de revues que de romans.
Cette librairie vend plus de revues que la boutique voisine.
answers: Cette librairie vend plus de revues que de romans.
practice.explanation: Que de romans introduces a second noun category; que la boutique voisine introduces another seller.

practice.prompt: Complete 'as many seats as': Cette salle a ___ sièges que l'autre. Write only the two words before sièges.
practice.explanation: The required words are autant de; que is already supplied after the noun.

practice.prompt: Supply the superlative article: C'est la rue ___ plus calme du quartier.
practice.explanation: Ranking feminine rue among streets requires la.

practice.prompt: Use the past subjunctive of recevoir for an evaluative judgement: C'est le plus beau cadeau que j'___ .
practice.explanation: Past subjunctive expresses completed experience under the specified evaluation.

practice.prompt: In le meilleur repas que j'aie jamais mangé, what does jamais mean?
practice.explanation: This experiential affirmative comparison is not a negation.

practice.prompt: Supply 'less' before the noun bruit, including the required preposition: Ce modèle fait ___ bruit que l'ancien.
practice.explanation: Noun comparison uses moins de.

practice.prompt: Supply 'more' before the noun énergie, including elision: Cette tâche demande ___ énergie que l'autre.
practice.explanation: De elides before énergie.

practice.prompt: Supply the equality word before an adjective: Ce train est ___ rapide que l'autre.
practice.explanation: Aussi compares adjectives; autant de compares nouns.

practice.prompt: Supply the comparison-set preposition and contracted article: C'est le pont le plus ancien ___ pays.
practice.explanation: De + le pays becomes du pays.

practice.prompt: Supply meilleur agreeing with solutions: Ces solutions sont ___ .
practice.explanation: Feminine plural adjective.

practice.prompt: Use lire in the past subjunctive with agreement: C'est la meilleure analyse que nous ___ .
practice.explanation: Ayons + lue; que refers to feminine singular analyse.

practice.prompt: Use pouvoir in the present subjunctive: C'est le tarif le plus bas que vous ___ proposer.
practice.explanation: A present capacity, not past completion.

practice.prompt: Rank different women: Elle est ___ plus attentive du groupe. Supply the article.
practice.explanation: A feminine person is ranked among others.

practice.prompt: Build the noun phrase 'the quietest room in the building' with salle, calme and bâtiment. Keep calme after salle, use plus and definite articles; no sentence or punctuation.
answers: la salle la plus calme du bâtiment
practice.explanation: Post-noun adjective repeats the feminine article, and de + le bâtiment contracts to du bâtiment.

practice.prompt: Build 'the third-largest city in the country' using troisième, grand, ville, pays and plus. Keep grand before ville; no sentence or punctuation.
answers: la troisième plus grande ville du pays
practice.explanation: Ordinal rank precedes plus; grande agrees with ville and the comparison set uses du pays.

practice.prompt: Supply the two-word expression containing de after the noun, meaning 'two extra places': Il reste deux places ___.
practice.explanation: De plus is the requested expression; en plus or supplémentaires could express a similar idea without this constraint.

practice.prompt: Compare the same woman's attention at different times, using invariable le: C'est à neuf heures qu'elle est ___ plus attentive. Supply the article.
practice.explanation: The prompt specifies degrees of the same subject, not a ranking among women.

practice.prompt: Use voir in the past subjunctive with agreement: C'est la plus belle exposition que tu ___ .
practice.explanation: Preceding feminine singular object triggers vue.

practice.prompt: Is indicative forbidden in every relative clause near a superlative?
choices: No; it can assert facts or define the factual comparison set.
Yes; le plus always forces every later verb into subjunctive.
answers: No; it can assert facts or define the factual comparison set.
practice.explanation: Construction and stance matter, not proximity to le plus.

production_task.prompt: Recommend one of two meeting venues. Compare a noun quantity, rank a quality within a named set, and give one explicitly personal evaluation with a past-subjunctive relative. Acknowledge one drawback.
production_task.model_answer: La salle du parc offre autant de places que celle de la mairie, mais on y entend moins de bruit. C'est la salle la plus lumineuse du quartier. C'est aussi l'espace le plus accueillant que j'aie visité. En revanche, le trajet est un peu plus long.
production_task.translation: The park room offers as many places as the town-hall room, but less noise can be heard there. It is the brightest room in the neighbourhood. It is also the most welcoming space I have visited. On the other hand, the journey is a little longer.
rubric: Noun quantities use `de` and an explicit comparison.
The superlative names its comparison set and agrees correctly.
The past subjunctive expresses the requested personal evaluation.
The recommendation weighs a real drawback rather than using only extremes.
